question: A team is evaluating the MCP connector for the Messages API to connect Claude to several internal servers. Which of the following statements about the MCP connector are accurate? (Select all that apply.)
options: A) Only one MCP server can be connected per Messages API request; multiple servers require separate requests.
B) The connector automatically converts every connected server's resources into Files API uploads for later reuse.
C) The connected MCP server must be publicly reachable over HTTPS using Streamable HTTP or SSE transport.
D) Local STDIO-based MCP servers can be connected directly by including their local process path in the mcp_servers array.
E) Of the full MCP specification, only tool calls are currently supported through the connector; resources and prompts are not.
F) Data exchanged with connected MCP servers is not eligible for Zero Data Retention and follows the standard retention policy.
correct_answers: C) The connected MCP server must be publicly reachable over HTTPS using Streamable HTTP or SSE transport.
E) Of the full MCP specification, only tool calls are currently supported through the connector; resources and prompts are not.
F) Data exchanged with connected MCP servers is not eligible for Zero Data Retention and follows the standard retention policy.
explanations: Incorrect. A single request can include multiple MCP servers, each with its own entry in mcp_servers and a corresponding MCPToolset.
Incorrect. The connector does not automatically convert server resources into Files API uploads; that conversion is unsupported by the connector itself.
Correct. The server must be publicly exposed over HTTP, supporting either Streamable HTTP or SSE transport.
Incorrect. Local STDIO servers cannot be connected directly through the MCP connector; only publicly reachable HTTP-based servers are supported.
Correct. Of the MCP specification's features, only tool calls are currently supported by the connector; resources and prompts are not.
Correct. The MCP connector is not eligible for Zero Data Retention, and exchanged data follows the standard retention policy.
